scenes.heading: Data Sources
scenes.narration: Data sources are the systems and channels that produce the raw data a pipeline collects and processes.

scenes.heading: Common data sources
bullets: Files such as logs, CSVs, and exports
scenes.narration: Operational databases are a primary source because they hold an application's live data. APIs let engineers pull data from external services the business relies on. Event streams capture user activity as it happens, moment by moment. Files like logs and exports carry batch data from many systems, and sensors and IoT devices generate continuous machine-produced readings.

scenes.heading: From source to pipeline
scenes.narration: An engineer first identifies each source and understands its format and update frequency. They then choose an appropriate extraction method, whether batch pulls or streaming. Finally the data is ingested and landed in central storage, ready for the rest of the pipeline.

scenes.text: Knowing your data sources and how they behave is the first step in designing any reliable pipeline.
scenes.narration: Every pipeline starts by understanding its sources, because their formats, volumes, and update patterns shape every downstream decision.
